Albert Einstein (1879–1955) was a German-born theoretical physicist who is widely ranked among the most influential scientists of all time. Best known for developing the **theory of relativity**, he also made foundational contributions to quantum mechanics and reshaped humanity's understanding of space, time, gravity, and the universe.

![Albert Einstein in 1951](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/46/Albert_Einstein_sticks_his_tongue.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

---

## Key Scientific Contributions

*   **Special Relativity (1905):** Postulated that the laws of physics are the same for all non-accelerating observers and that the speed of light in a vacuum is regardless of the motion of all observers. This led to the famous mass-energy equivalence formula: 
    $$E = mc^2$$
*   **General Relativity (1915):** A revolutionary geometric theory of gravitation stating that what we perceive as the force of gravity arises from the curvature of space and time caused by mass and energy.
*   **The Photoelectric Effect (1905):** Proved that light can be thought of as streams of particles (photons) rather than just waves, laying the quantum groundwork that earned him the **1921 Nobel Prize in Physics**.

---

## Life and Legacy

|   |   |
| :--- | :--- |
| Born | March 14, 1879, in Ulm, Kingdom of Württemberg, German Empire |
| Died | April 18, 1955 (aged 76) in Princeton, New Jersey, US |
| Citizenship | German, Swiss, American |
| Key Institutions | University of Zurich, Prussian Academy of Sciences, Institute for Advanced Study (Princeton) |

Beyond his scientific achievements, Einstein became a global cultural icon of genius and a passionate advocate for pacifism, civil rights, and international cooperation.
